correctness.rationale: For fixed point of 1→101, 0→000, length n=3^k and B=2^k, the ones in C_k occupy positions f(j)=2Σ epsilon_i(j)3^i. Every length-n factor is 0^n or a zero-padded prefix/suffix of C_k because the base word has no 11 and contains 00,01,10. Counting scattered 01 using first t one-positions gives exactly the two progressions t(m-t)-P_t and t(n-m)+P_t, m∈[f(t-1)+1,f(t) or n]. Counting their intersections using m+m’=n+t+2P_t/t proves b_{c,2}(3^k)=2·3^k+1−ΣO_t. For k≥3, t=3·2^{k-2} and the explicit paired lengths produce 2·3^{k-3}+1 distinct nonidentical factor pairs with equal binomial profiles; their differing last-one positions exclude literal identity. Independent brute-force scattered-subsequence profiles of actual substitution words for k=1..6 match the arithmetic family exactly. That finite test does not establish the all-k claim.
residual_risks: Formula is a 2^k-term explicit sum rather than a simplified closed form.
No assertion covers all lengths or higher-order k-binomial equivalence.
